# FDG6019

> AVOID naming base classes with a “Base” suffix if the class is intended for use in public APIs.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 6.2 Base Classes.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG6019
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Remove the 'Base' suffix from '{0}', which a public API uses as a type

Library only: the text is about classes intended for use in public APIs. FDG6019 reports an unsealed, nonstatic, externally visible class whose name ends with the word Base (FooBase, not Database) when an externally visible member, delegate or generic type of the same compilation uses it in its signature: the return, parameter, property, indexer, field or event type, or a constraint of a type parameter, also as an array element type or a type argument, the way the GetFilenames method of the body returns Collection<string>. A class that the compilation uses only as a base class is not reported, nor one that only a constraint of its own type parameters names (EntityBase<TSelf> where TSelf : EntityBase<TSelf>), nor uses in other assemblies, and members that the compiler declares do not count. CA1711 does not report the Base suffix (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Renaming a public class breaks callers, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

For example, despite the fact that `Collection<T>` is designed to be inherited from, many frameworks expose APIs typed as the base class, not as its subclasses, mainly because of the cost associated with a new public type.

```csharp
public Directory {
  public Collection<string> GetFilenames(){
     return new FilenameCollection(this);
     }

  private class FilenameCollection : Collection<string> {
     ...
  }
}
```

The fact that `Collection<T>` is a base class is irrelevant for the user of the `GetFilename` method, so the “Base” suffix would simply create an unnecessary distraction for the user of the method.
